SB305.headline: Moves the alcohol-content cutoff between the two vinous liquor tax rates from 14% to 16%.

SB306.headline: Requires property owners' associations to file key documents online with TREC for public access.

SB307.headline: Removes the 18-member cap on the Central Texas Water Alliance board while keeping a five-member minimum.

SB308.headline: Creates criminal offenses for making or dealing in 3D-printed firearms and for sharing schematics to make them.

SB309.headline: Prohibits insurers from using credit information to make specified personal insurance decisions or set premiums.

SB31.headline: Requires medical assistance for applicants eligible for federal matching funds if voters approve a constitutional amendment.

SB310.headline: Changes public-school funding to use enrollment, raises the basic allotment, and adjusts it annually for inflation.

SB311.headline: Requires HHSC-licensed health facilities to verify job applicants before making an offer.

SB312.headline: Moves complaints against the family services department to the health commission’s ombudsman office for handling and tracking.

SB313.headline: Creates private-market health coverage assistance for some low-income people and changes Medicaid services and benefits.

SB314.headline: Extends the Harris County Hospital District’s health care provider program through 2029.

SB315.headline: Requires senior independent living communities to arrange equipment maintenance after a power outage.

SB316.headline: Creates a council to review foster care placements and complaints about placements of children in state care.

SB317.headline: Requires backup power in certain tax-credit housing developments for residents 55 and older.

SB318.headline: Bars health care providers from accepting payments for referring people to unlicensed group homes.

SB319.headline: Requires group homes to keep applicants’ and employees’ criminal history records.

SB32.headline: Requires a permit before construction begins on large computational load sites and certain major changes to them.

SB320.headline: Requires certain dialysis facilities to keep 72 hours of emergency power available and update their emergency plans.

SB321.headline: Prohibits landlords from keeping certain rental properties in unsafe or uninhabitable condition and lets county attorneys seek penalties.

SB322.headline: Requires a study of racial profiling by Texas peace officers and recommendations for policies to reduce it.

SB323.headline: Creates an independent office to oversee confinement conditions and offender treatment in Texas prisons.

SB324.headline: Raises the maximum municipal fine for illegal refuse dumping from $4,000 to $10,000.

SB325.headline: Sets distance limits for certain concrete plants and crushing facilities near homes, schools, businesses, and parks.

SB326.headline: Creates a Texas automobile insurance public option with minimum and optional coverage for eligible drivers.

SB327.headline: Bars most transfers of certain semiautomatic rifles to people under 21 and makes violations a felony.

SB328.headline: Restricts certain vaping and tobacco retailers from operating near schools and preschools.

SB329.headline: Creates a misdemeanor offense for disruptive or threatening conduct on or near school or day-care property after a request to leave.

SB33.headline: Requires separate transmission cost rates for certain computational load site customers.

SB330.headline: Exempts certain listed items under $100 from sales tax when sold on Veterans Day, starting in 2028

SB331.headline: Lets applicants and protected witnesses join protective-order hearings remotely when they request it in writing, unless the court finds good cause to deny it.

SB332.headline: Requires health care providers to generally bill patients within 90 days of service or identifying who is responsible.

SB333.headline: Requires building and construction contractors and subcontractors to cover each employee with workers’ compensation insurance.

SB34.headline: Lets counties zone unincorporated areas and require permits for certain large computing facilities

SB35.headline: Requires ERCOT’s independent organization to share information about large load customers with the Texas Water Development Board.

SB36.headline: Bars local development agreements and certain tax breaks for data centers beginning September 1, 2027.

SB37.headline: Requires school districts to offer tuition-free, full-day prekindergarten to children age four and older

SB38.headline: Creates no-interest loans for eligible students at public institutions, with rules for eligibility, repayment, and forgiveness.

SB39.headline: Creates Texas Promise grants to help eligible students pay tuition and fees for two-year programs and bachelor’s degrees.

SB40.headline: Gives eligible college students a sales tax break on qualifying books during seven-day periods in January and August.

SB41.headline: Restricts certain retailers from setting customer-specific prices for goods available through SNAP.

SB42.headline: Requires online ticket sellers to show the total price and fees before buyers select tickets.

SB43.headline: Requires covered state agencies to post open-meeting recordings and notices online, with some also livestreaming meetings.

SB44.headline: Limits livestreaming and other videography in voir dire and proceedings involving certain victims.

SB45.headline: Lets eligible siblings of certain military members receive public college tuition and fee exemptions.

SB46.headline: Requires a disclosure on certain political ads that show an officeholder or candidate doing or saying something unreal.

SB47.headline: Lets courts block certain depositions and civil cases when they are used to harass, intimidate, or control an alleged victim

SB48.headline: Gives employees affected by family violence up to 15 workdays off for medical, legal, or safety needs

SB49.headline: Directs border security efforts and creates grants for border-region courts and colleges.

SB50.headline: The bill would restrict credit-card network practices and cap fees for some large card issuers.

SB51.headline: Lets public retirement systems offer up to $1 million to survivors of eligible peace officers who die on duty

SB52.headline: Lets courts restrict nonconsensual remote control of devices affecting protected people’s homes, vehicles, or property and adds related offenses.

SB53.headline: Expands crime victims’ compensation eligibility for people injured while trying to prevent a criminal offense.

SB54.headline: Makes emergency medical services balance-billing protections expire only after a federal prohibition takes effect and the attorney general publishes a finding.

SB55.headline: Continues certain protections against emergency medical services billing through September 1, 2029.

SB56.headline: Bars defined pet stores from selling dogs and cats while allowing qualifying groups to hold adoption showcases in store space.

SB57.headline: Creates a Texas Seal of Biliteracy for qualifying public high school graduates and records it on their diplomas and transcripts.

SB58.headline: Lets certain local sponsors build or maintain small erosion and flood-control dams without a water permit

SB59.headline: Requires inspectors to report abandoned or deteriorated water wells found during septic system inspections.

SB60.headline: Changes when jurors must answer yes or no on sentencing issues in capital cases.

SB61.headline: Requires a certified Spanish translation of a colonia home-purchase contract when the buyer requests one.

SB62.headline: Creates state licensing rules for reroofing contractors and requires licensed contractors to disclose their license number and provide written contracts.

SB63.headline: Requires registration and training for people doing covered elevator work and limits how apprentices may work.

SB64.headline: Creates a training certificate for employed sanitation workers who are not yet eligible for full sanitarian registration.

SB65.headline: Lets off-highway vehicles operate on qualifying beaches under the stated land and safety rules

SB66.headline: Requires a study and pilot to help college students earn industry-recognized credentials.

SB67.headline: Limits how many home loans a property owner can make while using an exemption from mortgage licensing.

SB68.headline: Expands which counties can clarify a public interest in certain roads

SB69.headline: Lets commissioners courts in certain border counties abolish the appointed purchasing-agent office and employ a county purchasing agent.

SB70.headline: Lets local governments include advice and help with using property in personal-property contracts

SB71.headline: Lets most counties donate surplus property without first finding that a sale would likely fail or cost too much.

SB72.headline: Adds the Parks and Wildlife Department director and updates other seats on the Texas Groundwater Protection Committee.

SB73.headline: Requires state agencies to update internal-audit coverage, reporting practices, and professional standards.

SB74.headline: Requires a study of state-agency marketing costs and the possible savings from consolidating marketing services.

SB75.headline: Changes meeting schedules for some county bail bond boards and keeps licenses active while certain renewals await a decision.

SB76.headline: Exempts casual sellers and incidental recyclers of used auto parts from state regulation and expands what recyclers must remove from vehicles.

SB77.headline: Requires searchable or sortable electronic public information when requested and expands what counts as public information.

SB78.headline: Lets eligible municipalities convert a sports and community venue tax to an economic-development tax with voter approval

SB79.headline: Creates a nine-member commission to draw Texas congressional and legislative districts.

SB80.headline: Bars people under 21 from buying or possessing assault weapons and from being offered or transferred them.

SB81.headline: Makes immunization registry inclusion the default, with a right to request exclusion.

SB82.headline: Requires a veteran discount program for electronic toll customers on State Highway 130, funded by toll revenue.

SB83.headline: Lets qualifying cosmetologists seek licenses recognized in other compact states

SB84.headline: Allows eligible candidates to request an initial recount of paperless electronic voting results without giving a specific ground.

SB85.headline: Lets the water development board fund platting costs to prepare older areas for public water or sewer connections

SB86.headline: Revises who serves on the Texas lottery advisory committee and adds members with law-enforcement, legal, or financial expertise.

SB87.headline: Exempts certain testing equipment for substances in Penalty Group 1-B from a drug offense provision.

SB88.headline: Requires birthing facilities to add congenital CMV testing to newborn hearing screening, with exceptions and a parent option to decline.

SB89.headline: Requires public school campuses to report overdoses and protect students’ identifying information.

SB90.headline: Limits when child-care providers may deny services to children with disabilities and requires inclusive-care practices and parent information.

SB91.headline: Requires audio recording in covered special education settings and expands recording retention and access.

SB92.headline: Requires schools to give parents information about disability services and benefits at every committee meeting

SB93.headline: Requires school districts to set weekly unstructured playtime in recess policies.

SB94.headline: Lets school safety funds pay for educator training in classroom behavior management.

SB95.headline: Adds lactation rooms to places where people are considered to have privacy when disrobing.

SB96.headline: Creates a grant program for higher education research, education, and producer assistance in regenerative agriculture.

SB97.headline: Expands public school civics lessons to cover courts, the judiciary, and government organization.

SB99.headline: Repeals requirements for certain sheriffs to work with ICE and ends new grants for those agreements.

SCR1.headline: Designates October 15 as Lobular Breast Cancer Awareness Day in Texas.

SCR2.headline: Urges Congress to propose an amendment allowing limits on spending to influence campaigns, elections, and ballot measures

SJR10.headline: Lets voters decide whether Texas may allow retroactive civil claims arising from child sexual abuse

SJR11.headline: If voters approve, the amendment would let the Legislature authorize and regulate casino gaming and sports wagering.

SJR12.headline: Lets the Kickapoo Tribe operate covered games under a compact if voters approve the amendment.

SJR13.headline: Lets the Kickapoo Tribe offer certain gaming on designated Texas land if voters approve and Texas later authorizes it.

SJR14.headline: Lets lawmakers set a lower appraisal limit for qualifying residence homesteads if voters approve the amendment

SJR15.headline: Lets voters approve using certain highway-fund revenue for transit, bike paths, and sidewalks.

SJR6.headline: Requires Texas to provide medical assistance to applicants eligible for federal matching funds if voters approve the amendment.

SJR7.headline: Sets new rules for when lawmakers can introduce bills and hold hearings during a regular session

SJR8.headline: Creates a commission to draw Texas’s congressional and state legislative district maps.

SJR9.headline: Creates a commission to draw Texas congressional and legislative districts after each census.
